about: The San Francisco Ferry Building (1896-1898, A. Page Brown), drawn by eo-landmarks ferry_building.rs on the city record it replaces. Every measured value names its source below; every value under `inferred` has no published measurement and is a proportion chosen to fit the measured ones (marked INFERRED in the code).

sources.record: public/data/sf/sf-city.json.gz detailBuildings id 558731934 (OpenStreetMap way 558731934, building=terminal, height=15; ODbL 1.0, (c) OpenStreetMap contributors; see public/data/sf/sf-city.NOTICE.txt). Surveyed game metres (x east, z south) before the ground-plan scale.
sources.osm-parts: OpenStreetMap building:part ways of the Ferry Building, fetched 2026-11-18 through the Overpass API (ODbL 1.0, (c) OpenStreetMap contributors): 24460886 (main body, height 16.1), 404449724 (tower shaft, 43.5 m), 406710833 (50.5 m), 406710834 (54.2 m), 406710835 (60.5 m), 406710836 (64.5 m), 406710837 (68.2 m, round), 406710838 (70 m, roof:shape=dome), 406710839 (83.1 m, the flagstaff). Plan sizes are the parts' extents along and across the record's long axis, projected with the sf-city projection (meta.projection).
sources.wikipedia: San Francisco Ferry Building, en.wikipedia.org (read 2026-11-18): 245-foot (75 m) clock tower; four clock dials 22 feet (6.7 m) in diameter; the 660-foot (200 m) Great Nave; 22 nave arches per side.
sources.noehill: San Francisco Landmark No. 90, noehill.com/sf/landmarks/sf090.asp (read 2026-11-18): 659 feet long as built; eleven-foot minute hand; seven and one-half foot hour hand; tower modelled on the Giralda of Seville; a flagstaff surmounts the tower.
sources.architecture-sf: architecturesf.blogspot.com/2009/05/ferry-building-1896-1898.html (read 2026-11-18): the western front in Colusa sandstone, arcades spanning the full width of both the lower and upper stories, paired Corinthian columns on the entrance pavilion.
sources.cdmg-191: California Division of Mines and Geology Bulletin 191 (1966), as quoted by quarriesandbeyond.org (read 2026-11-18): Colusa sandstone is blue-gray and buff, weathering to light brown.
sources.polyhaven-sandstone: Poly Haven 'White Sandstone Blocks 02' (CC0; native/assets/cc0-manifest.json; the scan the kit's limestone-ashlar finish draws): a 2 m x 2 m tile of eleven courses (counted on its albedo), 0.18 m a course.

tower.source: osm-parts (centre and stage extents), wikipedia (245 ft to the finial), osm-parts 406710839 (the flagstaff top)

stages.note: shaft: 12.3 x 11.3 m in OSM, drawn square at their mean

body.source: osm-parts 24460886 (parapet top); wikipedia (22 nave arches per side over the surveyed frontage)

stone.source: cdmg-191 (blue-gray and buff, weathering to light brown) and architecture-sf (Colusa sandstone front)
stone.note: a multiply on the kit ashlar's #d6cbb6 bake (linear 0.67, 0.60, 0.47), taking it to a cleaned buff-grey (linear 0.54, 0.52, 0.47, albedo about 0.5)

inferred.note: INFERRED: no published elevation drawing was available; proportions fit the 16.1 m parapet, the 245 ft tower and the 22-bay frontage.

detail.source: INFERRED unless a source is named: no published elevation drawing or stone schedule was available. The course is the period's dimension-stone ashlar, about two feet; the scan (polyhaven-sandstone) is drawn at that course. --no-ferry-building-detail draws without this block.

relief.source: INFERRED: no published elevation, window schedule or glazing record was available. The float glass's roughness is the near-mirror of drawn glass (F0 4 %, n = 1.52, the same dielectric the second pass names); the frame sizes are those of a period steel or timber sash with its glazing bars standing proud of the glass. --no-facade-relief draws without this block.
